title: Nvidia and SK Group Unveil $500 Billion AI Initiative at South Korea Summit
excerpt: Samsung and SK Hynix are set to announce major chip supply deals with U.S. tech companies as South Korean President Lee Jae Myung courts Silicon Valley's biggest names in San Francisco.
body:
• Nvidia and SK Group unveiled a $500 billion-plus AI initiative spanning data centres and next-generation memory chips
  • SK Telecom will build a 2-gigawatt data centre powered by Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips and SK Hynix's HBM4 memory, due online in 2027
  • Samsung and SK Hynix are expected to announce long-term memory chip supply contracts with U.S. tech companies
  • South Korean President Lee met CEOs of Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Broadcom at a San Francisco AI summit

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung hosted a landmark AI summit in San Francisco on Friday, bringing together the heads of Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Broadcom with South Korea's top business leaders in a push to position the country as a global AI powerhouse.

On the sidelines of the summit, Nvidia and SK Group — South Korea's second-largest conglomerate — unveiled a $500 billion-plus AI initiative spanning large-scale data centres and next-generation high-bandwidth memory, according to Reuters.

The Deal

Under the agreement, SK Telecom plans to build a 2-gigawatt data centre powered by Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips and SK Hynix's HBM4 high-bandwidth memory chips. The facility is expected to come online in 2027.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=YQ-zjJfc2BA

The partnership builds on an existing relationship — SK Hynix is already Nvidia's largest memory supplier. "SK Hynix has been Nvidia's largest memory partner. SK Hynix will continue to be Nvidia's largest memory partner," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said after meeting SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, according to Reuters.

"We already procure and we buy from SK Hynix already billions and billions of dollars each year, and it's going to grow substantially."

— Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO

Samsung and SK Hynix Set to Announce Chip Deals

Ahead of the summit, South Korea's presidential policy adviser Kim Yong-beom told reporters that both Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix would announce large, long-term memory chip supply contracts with global technology partners.

https://x.com/nvidia/status/2080886765146321314

"We expect a lot of very large and meaningful figures to be announced," Kim said. "It is cementing the technology and economic partnership between South Korea and the United States."

Kim added that global technology companies would also announce "strategic investments" in AI data centres, though he did not provide specific details.

AI Ambitions on Display

About 150 executives, investors, researchers, and startup founders attended the summit. Lee separately met Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, and Broadcom CEO Hock Tan before delivering a keynote address unveiling a "San Francisco AI Declaration" outlining South Korea's AI ambitions.

"South Korea will make the leap as a key nation in the global AI supply chain," Lee said in his opening remarks.

Samsung Electronics Executive Chairman Jay Y. Lee, Hyundai Motor Group Executive Chair Euisun Chung, and Naver founder Lee Hae-jin also attended the event.

The Bigger Picture

The deals come as memory chip demand continues to surge, driven by AI training and inference workloads that require massive amounts of high-bandwidth memory. Samsung and SK Hynix, along with U.S.-based Micron Technology, dominate the global memory chip market.

Last week, Nvidia approved all three manufacturers to supply HBM4 chips for its Vera Rubin AI accelerator platform. The partnerships signal that the competition for AI infrastructure is shifting from software to the physical layer of chips, memory, and power.

For India's technology sector, the ripple effects are significant. Indian IT services firms like HCLTech, Infosys, and TCS are deeply embedded in the semiconductor ecosystem as design and engineering partners. As AI data centre buildouts accelerate globally, demand for skilled engineers and chip design talent in India is expected to rise in parallel.

The summit also comes as South Korea navigates trade tensions with the U.S. — the chip supply deals could help Seoul strengthen its economic relationship with Washington at a time when tariffs and technology restrictions remain unpredictable.
nri_angle: Indian tech professionals in both the U.S. and South Korea are directly affected by the semiconductor supply chain deals that will shape AI infrastructure and hiring in the coming years.
